questions.q: How did the Meiji Restoration help Japan modernise rapidly?

answer.text: For long Japan had been ruled by the Tokugawa shogun, while the emperor was only a figurehead. In 1853 the American Commodore Perry forced Japan to open to trade, exposing its weakness before the Western powers.

In 1868 power was restored to the emperor in what is called the Meiji Restoration. The new leaders adopted the slogan of a rich country and a strong army, and set out to modernise Japan while keeping its traditions.
They built a modern army and navy, promoted industries and railways, reformed education on Western lines, introduced a constitution in 1889, and set up a modern banking system.
Within a few decades Japan became a strong industrial and military power, even defeating China and Russia.

answer: Thus the Meiji Restoration transformed Japan into a modern nation from above.

questions.q: Compare the paths to modernisation taken by China and Japan.
answer: China and Japan both faced the challenge of Western power but followed very different paths to modernisation.

answer.text: Japan modernised under its own leadership through the Meiji Restoration. It borrowed Western technology and institutions while preserving its traditions, and its transformation was rapid, orderly and directed from the top by the state.

China's road was far more turbulent. The Qing empire was humiliated in the Opium Wars and by unequal treaties. Reform failed, and the monarchy was overthrown in the revolution of 1911, when Sun Yat-sen founded a republic. After decades of conflict, the Communists under Mao Zedong established the People's Republic in 1949, and later Deng Xiaoping opened the economy.
Thus Japan modernised through controlled reform, while China did so through revolution and upheaval.

answer: Both became major powers, but by opposite routes.

questions.q: How did Japan's modernisation affect its society and its role in the world?

answer.text: after the Meiji Restoration reshaped its society and made it a world power.

list: Industry, railways, a modern army and a national education system were built quickly
Society changed as new classes of industrialists and workers arose and old feudal ranks were abolished

answer.lead: It changed Japan's place in the world.

list: It became the first Asian country to industrialise and to defeat a European power, Russia, in war
But its growing military strength led to imperial expansion in Asia, with grave consequences later

questions.q: Why did China follow a different and more difficult path to modernisation than Japan?

answer.text: struggled to modernise where Japan succeeded quickly, for several reasons.

list: China was weakened by foreign powers who forced unequal treaties on it and seized trading rights
Its huge size, and a conservative imperial court, made rapid reform far harder

answer.lead: Its path was one of upheaval.

list: The old empire fell in 1911, but instability, warlords and foreign pressure followed
China's modernisation came only after long struggle and revolution, unlike Japan's swift, state-led change
